note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found on imaging.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents after being referred by primary care physician for evaluation of a lung nodule. Patient initially presented to PCP with a cough of approximately three months duration. Cough began after patient was loading hay with horses, approximately 400 bales per day, followed by development of a cold which prompted the visit to PCP. PCP diagnosed bronchitis and obtained a chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia, which incidentally revealed a lung nodule. Subsequent CT scan confirmed the nodule. Patient reports the cough has since resolved. Denies current pain, shortness of breath, or fever.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain or shortness of breath. Denies fever. Cough has resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis. Previous smoking history, quit approximately seven years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 milligrams weekly for rheumatoid arthritis.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No previous personal history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises regularly, particularly biking on local trails. Previously smoked but quit seven years ago and has remained tobacco-free. Has horses and performs farm work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 124/76, heart rate 70, respiratory rate 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, afebrile. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Heart regular rate and rhythm without clicks, rubs, or murmurs. No extra beats appreciated. Extremities: skin pink, warm, and dry without edema to lower extremities. Mild swelling noted at knuckles of third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 centimeter smooth nodule in lateral aspect of right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right upper lobe lung nodule, incidentally found. Plan includes: (1) Pulmonary function tests to establish baseline lung function; (2) PET CT to determine if nodule is metabolically active; (3) Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery with removal of nodule and small portion of lung under general anesthesia, anticipated duration approximately 1.5 hours. Patient will be admitted postoperatively with chest tube, anticipated discharge postoperative day 1. Rheumatoid arthritis: Continue current follow-up with rheumatologist and continue methotrexate therapy as previously outlined.
